title.value: Search state databases for unclaimed property under old names

introduction.value: The poster asked Claude to search unclaimed property databases in every state they lived in, using their name and old names.

method.value: The poster had Claude search official unclaimed-property databases using their current and old names plus every state they had lived in. The prompt told it to use official sources such as MissingMoney.com and each state treasury site, then return any matches with the source, amount if shown, and the link to start a claim; a commenter added that each claim should cite the exact database row or page or be dropped.

outcome.value: The post presents this as a reliable way to surface forgotten funds tied to old addresses or past names, but it gives no personal recovery amount or success-rate numbers. Comments say Claude Cowork could run it, while one person said Gemini did not work for them.

notes.value: The main catch is to search and claim only through official sites; the post says charging a fee, percentage, subscription, or asking for bank login to release your money is a red flag.

source_text.body:
Search state databases for unclaimed property under old names
The poster asked Claude to search unclaimed property databases in every state they lived in, using their name and old names.
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
The poster had Claude search official unclaimed-property databases using their current and old names plus every state they had lived in. The prompt told it to use official sources such as MissingMoney.com and each state treasury site, then return any matches with the source, amount if shown, and the link to start a claim; a commenter added that each claim should cite the exact database row or page or be dropped.
How it went
The post presents this as a reliable way to surface forgotten funds tied to old addresses or past names, but it gives no personal recovery amount or success-rate numbers. Comments say Claude Cowork could run it, while one person said Gemini did not work for them.
Worth knowing
The main catch is to search and claim only through official sites; the post says charging a fee, percentage, subscription, or asking for bank login to release your money is a red flag.
Try it yourself
with
Claude in Chrome
Copy prompt
Search the official unclaimed property databases for each state I've lived in: [list of states]. Search under my name [full name] and previous names [maiden or old names], plus my past addresses [cities], and give me a table of any matches with amount, holder and claim link. Do not submit any claim or enter personal ID numbers, and pause and show me the details first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/PromptEngineering/comments/1vrij5c/about_1_in_7_people_have_unclaimed_money_sitting
source_text.scope: Captured case text; external linked articles and HTML excluded.

introduction.en: A community post proposes searching for forgotten property across former residences and names.
introduction.zh: 一篇社区帖子提出按曾居住地区及曾用名寻找遗忘财产。

method.en: The poster asked Claude to search official unclaimed-property databases across every state previously lived in, using both current and former names.
method.zh: 发帖者让Claude按现名及曾用名，检索所有曾居住州的官方未领取财产数据库。

method.en: Requested outputs included the source, any displayed amount and a claim-start link. A commenter proposed excluding matches without an exact database row or page citation.
method.zh: 要求返回来源、页面显示的金额及申领入口；评论者建议没有准确数据库行或页面引用的匹配应剔除。

outcome.en: No personal recovery amount or measured success rate was reported. Comments suggested Cowork could help, while one person reported an unsuccessful Gemini attempt.
outcome.zh: 没有报告个人追回金额或测量成功率；评论建议Cowork可做，一人则称Gemini尝试失败。

notes.en: The post emphasizes official sites such as MissingMoney and state treasuries, treating release fees or bank-login requests as warning signs. Actual Claude and suggested Claude in Chrome are separate labels.
notes.zh: 帖子强调MissingMoney及州财政部门等官方站点，把领取费用或银行登录要求视作警讯；实际Claude与推荐Claude in Chrome分别标记。
